patients.summary: Retired postal clerk with hypertension, type 2 diabetes and hyperlipidemia who joined in May 2024 and then had three acute ischemic strokes (June 2024, February 2025, December 2025), each admitted briefly and recovered without residual deficit. Aspirin was first added after the third stroke; statin never intensified.

documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Mr. Roberge phoned about membership. Says his old primary care doctor is retiring and the office is closing out its panel this summer. Has Medicare A and B. New patient slot booked 5/29 at 8:00 am, asked to come fasting for labs. Records release form emailed so we can pull his old chart.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

CC: Transferring care. Prior PCP retiring.

HPI: 67 y/o retired postal clerk here to establish. Carries three long-standing diagnoses: hypertension (roughly 15 yrs), type 2 diabetes (about 12 yrs), high cholesterol. All managed by his prior PCP, no specialists. Reports he takes his pills every day and rarely misses; wife sets up a weekly pill box. Doesn't check sugars at home with any regularity, last A1c he recalls was 'a bit over 7.' No hypoglycemia. No chest pain, dyspnea, claudication, numbness in feet, vision change. Came in fasting.

MEDS: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
ALLERGIES: none to medications.

PMH: HTN, T2DM, hyperlipidemia.
PSH: gallbladder removed 2005; inguinal hernia repair 2012.
FH: Father had a heart attack at 61. Mother had type 2 diabetes. Paternal grandfather had an ischemic stroke at 68.
SH: Married, lives with wife in Amherst. Retired from the post office (window clerk). Smoked for years, 25 pack-yrs, quit in 2010. Has a beer or a glass of wine once or twice a week. No other substances.

ROS: otherwise negative, 12 systems.

EXAM: Vitals as charted. Well-appearing, conversant.
HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no bruits, no thyromegaly.
CV RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear.
Abd soft, healed RUQ/umbilical port scars, healed groin scar, no hernia.
Ext: no edema. Feet: skin intact, monofilament sensation intact bilaterally, DP pulses 2+.
Neuro: alert, speech fluent, CN grossly intact, strength 5/5 x4, gait normal.

A/P:
1. Hypertension: reasonable control on lisinopril 20. Continue.
2. Type 2 diabetes: on metformin alone. A1c, CMP, urine microalbumin today. Continue metformin 1000 BID.
3. Hyperlipidemia: atorvastatin 40. Fasting lipids today.
4. Former smoker, quit 14 yrs ago. Not in a window for lung screening.
5. Health maintenance: HCV antibody today. Prior office records requested for colonoscopy and vaccine history. Will set up diabetic eye exam.

Refills sent for all three, 90-day supply. Follow-up after labs and records, roughly 3 months.

documents.title: Your recent labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mr. Roberge, all of your labs from Wednesday are back. A1c is 7-ish, which is close to where we want it for you. Kidney function and liver tests look fine and the urine protein screen is normal. Hepatitis C screen negative. Cholesterol: LDL is 100 on the atorvastatin. Nothing to change right now. We'll go over it more at your next visit.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
41 pages received via fax from patient's previous internal medicine office, covering 2016 to May 2024. Abstracted:
- Problem list: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia. Matches what pt reported.
- Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40. No recent dose changes.
- Surgical: cholecystectomy 2005, inguinal hernia repair 2012.
- Screening colonoscopy 9/2018: normal exam to cecum, no polyps; 10-year interval.
- Immunizations: Tdap 4/2019; Shingrix x2 (3/2021, 6/2021); PCV20 10/2023.
- Allergies: NKDA.
Vaccines entered into immunization history. Scanned under Media. Routed to PCP.

reports.text: Noncontrast axial CT of the head. No intracranial hemorrhage. Gray-white differentiation preserved. No mass, mass effect or midline shift. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age. No extra-axial collection. Calvarium intact. Visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells clear.

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
AREA HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Visit date: 06/30/2024
Patient: Arthur Roberge, 67 M

Chief complaint: Left side weak, speech slurred.

HPI: 67-year-old man who noticed his left arm and leg going weak and his words coming out thick about two hours before he got here. Known HTN, type 2 DM, hyperlipidemia. Says he has not missed any doses of lisinopril, metformin or atorvastatin. Lipids drawn by his PCP last month: TC 190, LDL 100, HDL 45, TG 150.

PMH: HTN, DM2, HLD. PSH: cholecystectomy 2005, inguinal hernia repair 2012.
Meds: lisinopril, metformin, atorvastatin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father MI at 61; mother DM2; paternal grandfather ischemic stroke at 68.
Social: ex-smoker, 25 pk-yr, quit 2010. 1-2 drinks weekly. Retired from the postal service.

Vitals: BP 155/90, HR 78, RR 16.
Exam: Left facial droop. Dysarthric speech. Strength reduced in left upper and left lower extremity. Remainder of exam unremarkable.

Imaging: CT head without contrast, no hemorrhage.

Impression: Acute ischemic stroke, right hemisphere presentation.
Disposition: Admitted to the hospitalist service for stroke care.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 06/30/2024, discharged 07/03/2024.

Diagnosis: Acute ischemic stroke.

Course: Admitted from the ED with left face/arm/leg weakness and dysarthria, head CT without hemorrhage. Deficits steadily improved over the stay. Ambulating independently at discharge, speech clearer.

Discharge medications (continued, no changes): metformin 1000 mg twice daily; lisinopril 20 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Discharged home with wife. Follow up with PCP within 1-2 weeks.

documents.title: Wife called re: admission
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt's wife called to let us know he was admitted yesterday after an ED visit for a stroke. She says his arm is already a little stronger this morning. Told her we'll request records and that he should be seen here within a week or two of discharge. She'll call when they have a discharge date. FYI to PCP.

conditions.label: History of stroke without residual deficits

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with wife one week after discharge from the hospital (6/30 to 7/3) for acute ischemic stroke: left face, arm and leg weakness with dysarthria, CT negative for bleed. Discharge summary and ED note reviewed.

Says he feels back to himself. Speech normal per wife since about day 2 in the hospital. Left hand grip 'all there.' Walking around the neighborhood. No headache, no new symptoms, no falls. Taking all three meds.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40. Hospital made no changes.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, fluent speech, no dysarthria. Face symmetric. Strength 5/5 all four limbs, no drift. Finger-nose normal. Gait steady.

A/P:
1. Ischemic stroke 6/30, recovered with no residual deficit on today's exam. Moved to history on the problem list. Continue current meds.
2. HTN: BP fine today on lisinopril.
3. T2DM, HLD: unchanged.
Reviewed stroke warning signs with both of them, call 911 for any new weakness or speech trouble. RTC November for diabetes check.

documents.title: Optometry diabetic eye exam
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

I saw your patient Arthur Roberge on 08/14/2024 for his annual diabetic eye examination.

Visual acuity corrected 20/25 OD, 20/25 OS. Pupils equal and reactive, no APD. IOP 15 mmHg each eye. Dilated fundus exam: clear media, healthy optic nerves, maculae flat and dry, no hemorrhages, microaneurysms or exudates in either eye.

Impression: type 2 diabetes with no diabetic retinopathy.
Recommend repeat dilated exam in 12 months.
Medications reviewed: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin. Allergies: NKDA.

Thank you for allowing me to participate in his care.
Optometry

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for seasonal shots. Afebrile, feeling well. Screening questions negative. High-dose flu given L deltoid, updated Pfizer COVID given R deltoid. VIS provided. Waited 15 min, no reaction. Lot numbers in the immunization record.

documents.title: Chronic Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Routine recheck. Doing well since the stroke in June, no recurrent symptoms. Admits the holidays started early, more sweets around the house. No lows. Good with meds. Flu and COVID shots done here in Oct.

O: vitals as charted. Speech normal, face symmetric, moves all extremities with full strength. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Feet without lesions, sensation intact.

A/P:
T2DM - A1c and BMP today. If up, talk diet first.
HTN - at goal, lisinopril 20.
HLD - atorvastatin 40.
Hx stroke - stable.
Follow up 3-4 months or sooner.

documents.title: A1c from this week
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Arthur, your A1c came back a little higher than in May, and your kidney numbers are stable. Let's give it until the next visit with less dessert and more walking and see where it lands before we think about adding anything.

documents.title: RE: A1c from this week
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Fair enough. My wife already hid the cookies. Thanks Doc.

documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
AREA HOSPITAL ED
Date of service: 02/26/2025
Pt: Arthur Roberge, 67 M

CC: Left-sided weakness, slurred speech x 2 hrs.

HPI: 67M with HTN, DM2, HLD and an ischemic stroke in June 2024 brought in after abrupt left-sided weakness and thick speech starting about 2 hours ago. Last known normal 3 hours before arrival. Wife at bedside says he has been reliable with metformin, lisinopril and atorvastatin.

PSH: cholecystectomy 2005; inguinal hernia repair 2012.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: father MI age 61; mother DM2; paternal grandfather ischemic stroke age 68.
SHx: former smoker (25 pack-years, quit 2010); 1-2 drinks/week; retired postal clerk.

VS: BP 155/90, HR 78, afebrile.
Exam: Left-sided facial droop. Weakness of the L arm and L leg. Dysarthria.

Labs: glucose 180, creatinine 1.2, INR 1.0, platelets 250.
CT head noncontrast: no hemorrhage.

Assessment: recurrent acute ischemic stroke.
Plan: admit, hospitalist service.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission: 02/26/2025. Discharge: 03/01/2025.

Principal diagnosis: Acute ischemic stroke (second event; first 06/2024).

Hospital course: Presented with left face, arm and leg weakness and dysarthria; head CT without hemorrhage. Neurologic deficits improved through the admission. At discharge walking without assistance, mild residual slurring that was improving.

Discharge medications, unchanged from home: metformin 1000 mg BID; lisinopril 20 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Disposition: home with wife. PCP follow-up within 1 week.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with his wife after a 2/26 to 3/1 admission for a second ischemic stroke, same picture as last June: left face/arm/leg weakness, slurred speech, CT without bleed. ED labs: glucose 180, creatinine 1.2, INR 1.0, platelets 250. ED note and discharge summary reviewed.

He says the speech cleared up the day after he got home. Wife agrees, says he sounds normal on the phone. No weakness, no trouble with buttons or stairs. Taking his meds; hospital did not change anything.

Exam: vitals as charted. Speech clear, no dysarthria. No facial asymmetry. Strength full and symmetric. No pronator drift. Normal heel-to-shin. Gait normal.

Assessment/plan:
1. Second ischemic stroke 2/26/2025, resolved without deficit on exam today. Problem list: history of stroke.
2. HTN on lisinopril 20 - continue.
3. DM2 - ED glucose 180 nonfasting. A1c due at the wellness visit in May.
4. HLD on atorvastatin 40 - continue.
Re-reviewed warning signs, 911 for anything new. Wife has the list on the fridge. Wellness visit in May.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
MEDICARE AWV (initial)

Health risk assessment completed in the portal and reviewed. Independent in all ADLs and IADLs. Still drives locally. Walks most mornings. No falls in the past year. Hearing and vision adequate, glasses for reading. Lives with wife, who is well.

Interval: no new neuro symptoms since the February stroke. Taking meds as prescribed.

Problem list reviewed: HTN, type 2 DM, hyperlipidemia, history of ischemic stroke x2 (6/2024, 2/2025), s/p cholecystectomy, former smoker.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

PHQ-2: 0. Cognition: no formal screen today; conversation and recall normal throughout visit. Advance directive: has a health care proxy (wife), copy to be brought in.

Exam: vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Neck no bruits. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Feet: intact skin, sensation intact to monofilament, pulses palpable. Neuro: fluent, symmetric face, strength 5/5, gait normal.

Screening/prevention:
- Colonoscopy 2018 normal, next 2028.
- Tdap 2019, Shingrix complete, PCV20 2023.
- Flu and COVID given here last October.
- HCV negative 2024.
- Diabetic eye exam 8/2024 without retinopathy; reminder for August.

Labs today: lipids, CMP, CBC, A1c, urine microalbumin.
Written personalized prevention plan given. Follow up 4-5 months.

documents.title: Wellness visit labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Roberge, your labs look steady. A1c improved a bit since November. Kidneys, liver, blood counts and urine protein are all normal. LDL is about where it was last year. Keep doing what you're doing.

documents.title: Optometry diabetic eye exam
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Re: Arthur Roberge, DOB 03/07/1957
Exam date: 08/13/2025

Annual dilated exam for type 2 diabetes. Best-corrected acuity 20/25 both eyes, unchanged. IOP 14 OD, 15 OS. Anterior segments quiet. Fundi: cup-to-disc 0.3 both eyes, vessels normal caliber, maculae flat, no hemorrhage, microaneurysm, exudate or neovascularization.

Assessment: no diabetic retinopathy either eye.
Plan: return in one year.
Current meds per patient: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin. Allergies: NKDA.

Optometry

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
AREA HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPT
DOS: 12/31/2025
Arthur Roberge, 68M

CC: Confused, speech slurred.

HPI: 68-year-old man with HTN, type 2 diabetes and hyperlipidemia, here about 10 months after his most recent ischemic stroke (also had one in 6/2024). His wife brought him in; she noticed him confused and slurring words beginning roughly 2 hours ago. According to her he has been taking all of his medicines and has not been sick lately.

Home meds: metformin 1000 mg PO BID; lisinopril 20 mg PO daily; atorvastatin 40 mg PO daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
PSH: cholecystectomy (2005), inguinal hernia repair (2012).
Family hx: father with MI at 61, mother with DM2, paternal grandfather with ischemic stroke at 68.
Social: quit smoking 2010 after 25 pack-years; drinks 1-2 a week socially; retired postal clerk.

Vitals: T 37.0 C (98.6 F), BP 160/90, P 88, RR 16.
Exam: Alert, anxious-appearing. Expressive aphasia. Right facial droop.

CT head without contrast: no hemorrhage, no mass effect.

Impression: acute ischemic stroke.
Disposition: admitted to medicine.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 12/31/2025 - Discharge 01/03/2026

Dx: Acute ischemic stroke (prior events 06/2024 and 02/2025).

Course: Admitted with expressive aphasia and right facial droop; CT head negative for hemorrhage or mass effect. Language improved steadily; at discharge naming and fluency near baseline per wife, face symmetric at rest.

Medications at discharge (no changes): metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Home with family. See PCP this week.

medications.drug: aspirin 81 MG Delayed Release Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily

documents.title: Post-Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit, accompanied by wife.

Hospitalized 12/31 to 1/3 with his third ischemic stroke, this time with word-finding trouble (expressive aphasia) and a right facial droop. CT without bleed or mass effect. Records reviewed. Discharged on the same three medicines.

Today: he says words come when he wants them again. Wife says he was searching for words for a day or two at home, none since the weekend. No weakness, no headache, no vision change. Eating and sleeping normally.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert and oriented, fluent, names objects and repeats a phrase without error. Face symmetric. Strength 5/5 x4, no drift, gait steady.

A/P:
1. Ischemic stroke 12/31/2025, third event, recovered on today's exam. Start aspirin 81 mg daily. Discussed bleeding precautions and taking it with food. Continue lisinopril, atorvastatin, metformin.
2. HTN, DM2, HLD - unchanged regimen.
Warning signs reviewed again. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: aspirin
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Picked up the baby aspirin. Is it OK to take it at the same time as the rest of my morning pills or should I space it out?

documents.title: RE: aspirin
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Good morning Mr. Roberge. Fine to take it with your other morning pills, ideally with breakfast. Let us know if you notice unusual bruising or dark stools.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
3 month f/u.

Tolerating aspirin, no bruising or GI upset. No neuro events since New Year's. Walking again now that the snow is gone. Diet 'mostly behaving.'

Meds: aspirin 81, metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40.

Exam: vitals as charted. Fluent speech, face symmetric, strength full. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.

Plan: A1c, BMP today. No med changes. Wellness visit in August with fasting labs.

documents.title: A1c result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news, Arthur: A1c is the best it has been since you joined us, and your kidney function and potassium are normal. See you in August.

documents.body: Renewal requests received for atorvastatin 40 mg daily and lisinopril 20 mg daily, 90-day supplies. Last BMP 4/8 normal. Routed, signed by PCP, sent with 1 refill to carry him to the August visit.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
MEDICARE AWV (subsequent) + chronic disease f/u

HRA reviewed. Independent, walking 30 min most days, no falls. Reading glasses only. Wife in good health; she remains his health care proxy.

Interval: no stroke symptoms since the 12/31 event. On aspirin since January without trouble. No lows.

Problems: HTN; DM2 without complications; hyperlipidemia; history of ischemic stroke (6/2024, 2/2025, 12/2025) without residual deficit; s/p cholecystectomy; former smoker.
Meds: aspirin 81 daily, metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

PHQ-2 0. Cognition grossly intact during visit, follows a multi-step conversation without lapses.

Exam: vitals as charted. Neck supple without bruit. RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft. Feet: no ulcers or calluses, monofilament intact, pulses 2+. Neuro: fluent, face symmetric, strength 5/5, gait normal.

Prevention: colonoscopy due 2028. Immunizations current through last fall; flu and COVID when available. Eye exam scheduled with optometry this month.

Fasting labs today: lipids, CMP, A1c, urine microalbumin. Continue current regimen. Return in about a month to go over labs and BP.

documents.title: Results from Friday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Arthur, labs from Friday are in. A1c is a touch higher than April but still in a reasonable range. Kidneys, liver and urine protein are normal. Cholesterol numbers are similar to last year. We'll talk it over at your September visit.

documents.title: RE: Results from Friday
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. Blame the corn on the cob. See you in Sept.
